message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; 1.00794 for protium) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Valence electrons** | 1 |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (²H, 0.02 %) – stable; Tritium (³H) – radioactive (half‑life 12.32 yr) |
| **State at STP** | Diatomic gas (H₂) |
| **Color / Odor / Taste** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless |
| **Density at STP** | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0899 kg m⁻³) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (−434.3 °F) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (–423.17 °F) |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas)** | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (≈14.304 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) |
| **Enthalpy of formation (gas)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| **Ionization energy (first)** | 1312 kJ mol⁻¹ (13.598 eV) |
| **Electron affinity** | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (0.754 eV) |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **Atomic radius** | 31 pm |
| **Molecular weight (H₂)** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 432 kJ mol⁻¹ (4.48 eV) |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive mixtures with air (4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| **Reactivity** | Forms covalent bonds with most elements; reacts with halogens, metals, and nonmetals; forms acids (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄) and hydrides (e.g., LiH, CaH₂) |
| **Hydrogen bonding** | Strong H–bond donor/acceptor; gives water its high surface tension, boiling point, and solvent properties |
| **Spectroscopic features** | Balmer series (visible lines), Lyman series (UV), Paschen series (IR); fundamental vibrational frequency ≈ 4401 cm⁻¹ (ν₁) |
| **Industrial uses** | Ammonia synthesis (Haber–Bosch), methanol production, petroleum refining, metal hydride production, hydrogenation of organic compounds, fuel cells, rocket propellant (LH₂/LOX), hydrogen storage research |
| **Energy applications** | Fuel cells (electrochemical conversion to electricity + water), hydrogen combustion (produces only water), hydrogen bombs (thermonuclear fusion) |
| **Biological relevance** | Essential component of amino acids, nucleic acids, ATP; participates in redox reactions (e.g., NAD⁺/NADH, FAD/FADH₂) |
| **Cosmological abundance** | ~75 % of elemental mass in the Universe; main constituent of stars and gas giants |
| **Safety** | Low density → tends to rise; forms explosive mixtures; requires careful handling and ventilation; tritium is radioactive and requires shielding |

---

### Quick Summary

- **Lightest element**: atomic number 1, mass 1.008 u.
- **Diatomic gas**: H₂ at room temperature and pressure.
- **Highly reactive**: forms covalent bonds, reacts with metals, halogens, acids, and oxidizers.
- **Key role in chemistry & biology**: part of water, organic molecules, enzymes, and energy carriers.
- **Industrial powerhouse**: central to ammonia, methanol, petroleum refining, hydrogenation, and emerging fuel‑cell technologies.
- **Cosmic significance**: most abundant element in the Universe, fuels stellar fusion.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
